Fred Finch Youth & Family Services is a great place to work. Year after year, our employees make the difference in helping those with mental health issues. Our team is currently looking for a CARE Manager
, whether you are just starting your career or a seasoned professional, you’ll be able to find the right position to help others.

Our Culture and Mission:

We envision Fred Finch as a healing-centered organization where our diverse staff at all levels feels at home. We are committed to creating an environment where employees can thrive, grow, and explore opportunities. Together, we actively work on diversity within our organization and the communities we serve.

Fred Finch Youth & Family Services partners with individuals and communities to provide culturally responsive services that cultivate mental and physical resilience and wellness.

The Enhanced Care Management (ECM) Program, operating under the umbrella of Fred Finch CARES, is a comprehensive care coordination benefit launched in July 2023 under CalAIM (California Advancing and Innovating Medi-Cal). ECM adopts a Whole Person Care Approach to healthcare, providing physical, behavioral, emotional, and social services to enhance care coordination and health outcomes. It is a care-coordination service offered to children, youth, and their families insured through Managed Medi-Cal. With a cross-regional services delivery model in both Northern and Southern California, ECM aligns and coordinates services across multiple systems of health and behavioral healthcare while addressing social determinants.

The CARE Manager oversees specific cases, coordinates health care benefits, provides education and facilitates client access to care in a timely and cost-effective manner. The CARE Manager collaborates and communicates with clients, caregivers/family support persons, and other providers to promote wellness, recovery, independence, resilience, and empowerment, while ensuring access to appropriate services and maximizing client benefit.

The CARE Manager also serves as an advocate for clients, an active client of the interdisciplinary team, a liaison with other programs and external health and social service providers in the community.

We provide essential support to those with intellectual and developmental disabilities, physical disabilities, autism, and mental health conditions - empowering them to thrive in their communities. Where barriers exist, we create pathways for inclusion and independence.

About our Adult Day Program:

Our Adult Day Program provides structured daytime services for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Individuals participate in skill-building, recreational, educational, and community-based activities that support independence, social connection, and personal goals. Staff work directly with individuals throughout the day, providing instruction, encouragement, personal care, behavioral support, and opportunities for meaningful participation.

The Program Coordinator (PC) is the lead Direct Support Professional (DSP) within the program. This is a hands-on working lead role, not a traditional administrative or supervisory position.

The PC works directly with individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities throughout the day, providing personal care, instruction, skill development, and positive behavioral support. The PC also helps keep the program running. jobs.description:
Job Description

Stanford Graduate School of Business is seeking a Program Manager, Engagement and Outreach, to support the school's most influential volunteer communities, including the Dean's Advisory Council and a growing portfolio of alumni boards and councils. This is a rare vantage point, offering the chance to work closely with some of Stanford GSB's most influential and engaged alumni leaders and to play a direct role in championing and stewarding the volunteers who provide strategic counsel, advocacy, and support for the school's mission.

The Program Manager owns operational management across board and council activity, including planning and executing logistics for high-visibility meetings, managing budgets, maintaining board and community management systems, and designing onboarding and offboarding experiences for council members. Operational logistics for the board and council member ecosystem span the full lifecycle, from prospective to current to former, including expanding engagement opportunities for former members, with ongoing attention to refining policies and procedures that improve the experience and efficiency of the program over time. Data hygiene is also a critical part of the job, with regular audits to ensure accuracy, alongside data analysis and reporting that surfaces engagement trends and informs recommendations shaping how these groups run. As a responsive, trusted point of contact for alumni volunteers, C-suite stakeholders, and their support staff, this person also partners closely with colleagues across External Relations and the broader campus community to coordinate support for boards and councils. There is also a firsthand opportunity to contribute to special projects and institutional initiatives as they arise.

This role is best suited to someone highly detail-oriented, energized by managing many moving pieces and relationships at once, and who genuinely enjoys the craft of meeting and event logistics. The ideal candidate communicates clearly across audiences, from senior alumni to internal teams, brings strong organizational skills, and approaches new systems and technologies with curiosity. This person brings genuine care, creativity, and a service-oriented mindset to the volunteer experience, always looking for thoughtful ways to make it exceptional. Sitting within a small Engagement and Outreach team, part of the broader External Relations team at Stanford GSB, the Program Manager reports to the Director, Engagement and Outreach. The position is a hybrid role requiring several days a week on campus with occasional evening and weekend availability to support events.

Unique Duties to this Role

Own end-to-end operational logistics for twice-yearly council meetings and occasional virtual gatherings, including venue coordination, materials and collateral, and day-of execution as applicable.
Manage board and volunteer management systems (e.g., Airtable, BoardEffect), including data hygiene, ongoing data audits, and platform administration, while developing strategies to strengthen community engagement through these tools.
Oversee the board and council lifecycle to ensure consistency and continuity of volunteer experience, engagement, and process.
Build and maintain relationships with executive assistants and support staff for C-suite-level stakeholders and Advisory Council members.
Lead an External Relations community of practice to align and strengthen support of boards and councils across the school.

Independently implement, administer and evaluate day-to-day activities of the unit, function or program by identifying and executing tasks and objectives, making recommendations that impact policies and programs, and assigning resources to achieve the goals of the program.

Represent the program or function as the key contact and subject matter expert within the department, unit or school. Commit resources and provide information and/or training. May also represent the program or function to external/internal stakeholders and constituencies.

The Care Coordinator works under the direction of the RN Care Manager and in collaboration with primary care providers, patients, caregivers, and interdisciplinary team members to support care management activities in the outpatient setting. This role assists with care coordination, transitions of care, chronic disease management, patient outreach, resource navigation, and documentation to improve patient outcomes, reduce avoidable utilization, and enhance the patient experience.

‎

How Will You Make An Impact & Requirements

‎

The Care Coordinator works under the direction of the RN Care Manager and in collaboration with primary care providers, patients, caregivers, and interdisciplinary team members to support care management activities in the outpatient setting. This role assists with care coordination, transitions of care, chronic disease management, patient outreach, resource navigation, and documentation to improve patient outcomes, reduce avoidable utilization, and enhance the patient experience.

The Care Coordinator may be a Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) or an experienced Medical Assistant (MA) with strong clinical knowledge and care coordination experience.

Program Goals

The Care Coordinator Supports The Following Organizational Goals

Prevent unnecessary emergency department visits and hospital admissions. Reduce 30-day hospital readmissions. Improve communication and care coordination between Primary Care Providers (PCPs), specialists, and acute care settings. Facilitate safe and effective transitions of care. Support advance care planning discussions and documentation. Assist patients and caregivers in identifying the most appropriate level of care following discharge. Improve patient engagement, self-management, and adherence to care plans.

Essential Responsibilities

Care Coordination

Assist the RN Care Manager in implementing and monitoring individualized patient care plans.
Perform monthly patient chart reviews to identify care gaps, preventive care needs, and opportunities for intervention.
Monitor and track follow-up appointments, referrals, diagnostic testing, and care plan goals.
Coordinate services among primary care providers, specialists, hospitals, skilled nursing facilities, home health agencies, and community organizations.
Collaborate with the healthcare team to ensure continuity of care across settings.

Patient Outreach and Engagement

Conduct telephonic outreach to patients and caregivers as directed by the RN Care Manager.
Assess barriers to care, including transportation, medication access, financial concerns, health literacy, and social determinants of health.
Encourage patient participation in care plans, preventive services, and chronic disease management programs.
Build and maintain trusting relationships with assigned patients and caregivers.

Transitions of Care

Support transition-of-care activities following emergency department visits, hospitalizations, and skilled nursing facility stays.
Assist with post-discharge follow-up, appointment scheduling, medication reconciliation support, and identification of ongoing care needs.
Ensure necessary services, equipment, and community resources are coordinated prior to or following discharge.
Communicate pertinent information to providers and care team members to facilitate timely interventions.

Patient Education

Reinforce education provided by the RN Care Manager and providers regarding:
Chronic disease management
Medication adherence
Preventive health measures
Self-management strategies
Community resources and support programs

Clinical Documentation and Record Management

Obtain and upload medical records, discharge summaries, consult notes, and test results from hospitals, specialists, skilled nursing facilities, and other providers.
Track care management activities, outreach attempts, patient outcomes, and quality metrics.

Resource Coordination and Advocacy

Assist patients in accessing appropriate clinical, social, behavioral health, and community-based services.
Maintain knowledge of local, state, and federal community resources.
Advocate for patient needs and promote patient-centered care.
Escalate clinical concerns to the RN Care Manager or provider as appropriate.

Education

Current Florida Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) license; or
Certified Medical Assistant (CMA/RMA) or equivalent Medical Assistant certification from an accredited program (Preferred).

Current BLS certification preferred.

MD Hyperbaric – Las Vegas provides advanced hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) to support healing, recovery, performance, and long-term wellness for the Las Vegas community. The Patient Care Coordinator & Hyperbaric Technician is a full-time, on-site role based at MD Hyperbaric in Las Vegas, NV. This position is responsible for welcoming clients, managing appointments, answering phones, and coordinating the flow of daily clinic operations to ensure a smooth and positive experience. The role includes conducting patient intake, reviewing medical information, explaining HBOT procedures, and supporting clinical staff with safe preparation and monitoring of clients during treatment sessions. The coordinator/technician maintains accurate documentation, follows established safety and infection-control protocols, and helps ensure compliance with physician-directed treatment plans. Daily responsibilities also involve communicating clearly with clients and team members, assisting with follow-up scheduling, and supporting general administrative and clinical tasks as needed.

Candidates should possess Care Coordination skills to support seamless patient workflows and collaboration with clinical staff.
Candidates should possess knowledge of Medical Terminology to understand treatment plans and communicate accurately with providers and clients.
Candidates should possess Patient Care skills, with a focus on empathy, professionalism, and safety during HBOT sessions.
Previous experience in a medical, wellness, or clinical setting (e.g., medical assistant, patient coordinator, or technician) is preferred.
Strong organizational abilities, attention to detail, and reliability in following protocols and documentation standards.
Comfort working with basic medical equipment, learning HBOT procedures, and adhering to safety and emergency response guidelines.
High school diploma or equivalent required; relevant healthcare certifications or training are a plus.
Ability to stand, walk, and assist clients throughout the day, and to work on-site during standard clinic hours.
Experience using a CRM (Customer Relationship Management) platform is a plus. Familiarity with GoHighLevel (GHL) or similar systems is preferred but not required.

Augusta University is Georgia's innovation center for education and health care, training the next generation of innovators, leaders, and healthcare providers in classrooms and clinics on four campuses in Augusta and locations across the state. Augusta University's distinct characteristics in education and research include real-world experiences and community engagement, as well as a culture of building community, corporate and government partnerships that address health, security, economic and societal concerns locally and across the state.

Augusta University

College/Department Information

The Augusta University School of Public Health was established in 2023 to address Georgia's distinct public health challenges through exceptional education, innovative research, and collaborative community engagement. We are leveraging the strengths of Georgia's only public academic medical center, combining public health expertise with clinical knowledge to train future public health leaders. Our school is comprised of three academic departments: Biostatistics, Epidemiology & Data Science, Community & Behavioral Health Sciences, and Health Management, Economics & Policy. Annually, we attract more than $6M in extramural funding.

Job Summary

Job Posting Refresh

The Public Health Data Analyst supports the School of Public Health (SPH) through statistical analysis, visualization, and data management for activities for research, evaluation, and grant-funded projects. This position will assist in administrative and technical work in support of a grant from the Centers for Disease Control.

It is expected this position will include travel across the target service area in Georgia from project implementation.

Responsibilities

The duties include, but are not limited to:

Statistical Analysis & Data Interpretation

Conduct qualitative and quantitative data analysis using appropriate statistical methods and software to support research objectives and evaluation frameworks. Interpret results and translate findings into meaningful insights for research teams, publications, and funding agencies.

Data Visualization & Reporting

Develop clear, accessible data visualizations, dashboards, and reports tailored to academic, clinical, and public health audiences. Communicate analytic findings in written, oral, and graphical formats for dissemination to internal and external stakeholders.

Data Management & Preparation

Design, implement, and maintain processes for data collection, cleaning, and integration across multiple datasets and sources. Develop and document reproducible workflows to ensure datasets are analysis -ready, accurate, and compliant with research standards. Maintain data dictionaries, coding structures, and analytic documentation to support transparency and reproducibility.

Training & Stakeholder Support

Coordinate and deliver training on data collection procedures and system use. Provide ongoing support to partners and project personnel.

Research Support & Scientific Output

Support development of literature reviews, IRB documentation, peer-reviewed manuscripts, abstracts, presentations, and grant applications.

Other

Perform other duties as assigned.

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university and 3 years of experience in data analytics, information systems, institutional research or other directly related field to include higher education functional units.

Preferred Qualifications

Preferred Educational Qualifications

Master's Degree from an accredited college or university and experience in community based participatory research; secondary data (ex:NHANES, NHIS, etc) or big data experience; strong computing skills (ex: SAS, Matlab, Perl, C++, etc)

Preferred Experience

A minimum of 3+ years' experience in data management or analysis.

Experience with implementation projects

Experience With Excel Functions And Statistical Software (SPSS, SAS)

Experience with qualitative data collection and analysis

Experience with qualtrics software for data collection

Experience with EHR data management, data abstraction, and data reporting

Ability to assess EHR data quality and identify potential issues

Ability to improve the quality of EHR data

Expertise in extracting population health data from EHRs

Expertise in integrating EBIs (e.g. provider reminders) into the EHRs

Experience with report writing

Ability to organize and store data with attention to completeness, security, and confidentiality (maintain data quality).

Strong analytic, communication, and problem-solving skills.

Abilities

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

Ability to maintain confidentiality

Excellent interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills

Detail-oriented with strong organizational and time management skills

Proficient in Microsoft Office and other computer software/databases or willingness to learn

Strong knowledge of SAS/SPSS, research and statistical methods, data manipulation and cleaning procedures

KNOWLEDGE
